source_snapshot.purpose_facts: The title indicates a non-fatal uncorrectable memory-error test under an NV CPU RAS set, but provides no platform, memory architecture, target, stimulus or acceptance details.
procedure_facts: Before-test text asks for recipe conformity and log clearing.
After-test text asks for result/photo collection and unexpected-log review.
missing_source_information: Exact NVIDIA CPU/product and host-memory architecture.
Authoritative injector, command/trigger and uncorrectable-non-fatal semantics.
Address, controller, channel, package-memory or other platform-specific target model and coverage.
Expected consumer action, native event/CPER/GHES identity, timeout, containment and no-system-reset rule.
Safety, data-isolation, recovery, restoration and pass/fail criteria.

original_test_intent.statement: The recoverable intent is to validate containment and reporting of an uncorrectable non-fatal host-memory error on an unspecified NVIDIA CPU platform; the source does not define the memory target, error consumption model, procedure or acceptance behavior.
must_preserve: Host memory rather than processor-core, GPU HBM, PCIe or storage error class.
Uncorrectable non-fatal rather than correctable or fatal severity.
NVIDIA CPU platform scope after exact product identification.
must_not_infer: That the platform is Grace, BlueField or another product.
That host memory is a removable DIMM or uses a conventional DIMM/channel map.
That generic Linux EINJ type 0x10 is implemented or is the intended injector.
An address/target, consumption workload, page-offline/process outcome, iteration count or native record.
That any hang, crash or system reset is acceptable for a non-fatal case.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly treats literal TBD Procedure and Criteria as a genuine semantic blocker, permits only read-only baselines and prohibits an invented memory injector.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 repeatedly assumes a DIMM/channel target model before the NVIDIA CPU architecture is known. That may be wrong for an NVIDIA Grace platform with package-integrated ECC LPDDR5X, and V2 does not require the owner to define whether/how the poisoned location is consumed and what non-fatal containment means.

related_records: Processor, Intel/AMD DDR, GPU HBM, BlueField and other NVIDIA memory-injection recipes cannot supply this row's missing platform-memory semantics.
applicable_history.precedence_application: The broad source title is preserved, but its two TBD fields prohibit importing a DIMM model or an injection flow from any neighboring case.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Maintain BLOCKED because stimulus, target and acceptance semantics are absent. Remove V2's premature DIMM/channel assumption, require the owner to define the actual NVIDIA host-memory topology and consumption/containment model, and allow only non-mutating discovery before a fresh review.

conditions_present: The host-memory error class, intended uncorrectable non-fatal severity, generic before/after collection steps and 10/10-minute estimates are known.
missing: Exact platform/memory architecture, injector, address/target and coverage, trigger/consumer, expected native record and containment, timeout, authorization, recovery and restoration.
provider: NVIDIA/ODM FAE supplies the exact platform memory-RAS specification and supported injector.
Test owner defines address/target coverage, trigger/consumer, non-fatal behavior and evidence criteria.
Platform/lab owner provides an isolated SUT, sacrificial data/workload, console/recovery and approvals.
safe_read_only_work: Inventory CPU/product, firmware, OS/kernel and actual host-memory topology without assuming DIMMs.
Inspect ACPI tables, kernel RAS configuration and advertised injection types without writing to any interface.
Export current native OS, BMC, memory-health and firmware RAS baselines without clearing logs.
prohibited_until_resolved: Log clear; BIOS/debug/module changes; memory allocation or poisoning; writes to injection parameters/triggers; vendor-tool injection; consumption of a suspect address; reset, retry or PASS/FAIL claim.
closure_evidence: Signed Procedure and Criteria replace both TBD fields for an identified platform and memory architecture.
A reviewed recipe defines target address/topology, coverage, stimulus/consumption, expected non-fatal containment/reporting, timeout, health and recovery.
Dedicated-SUT, data-isolation and per-action approvals are recorded.

revision_candidate.test_name: NVIDIA CPU Host-Memory Uncorrectable Non-Fatal Injection - Definition Required
revision_candidate.purpose: After an authoritative platform-specific recipe is supplied, inject a defined uncorrectable non-fatal error into each approved NVIDIA CPU host-memory target and verify target-correlated reporting, prescribed containment and continued system service without an unexpected fatal reset or hang. The current row is not executable.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Unresolved. The owner must identify the NVIDIA CPU/product, module/system, stepping, firmware, BIOS/BMC, OS/kernel and host-memory architecture. If Grace is selected, use its signed package-memory topology; do not assume removable DIMMs. Do not transfer BlueField, GPU-HBM or x86 DDR recipes.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Unresolved. The replacement recipe must define the platform-specific address/controller/channel/package-memory target, physical-to-logical mapping, protected sacrificial range, trigger/consumer, required targets and iterations. The 10/10-minute values are estimates, not timeouts or dwell durations.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Exact platform and memory architecture; authoritative NVIDIA/ODM RAS specification; supported injector/interface/tool version/hash; package/privilege and firmware/OS/kernel requirements; address/target map and coverage; protected sacrificial memory allocation; exact arm/trigger/consume sequence; expected uncorrectable-non-fatal event fields, CPER/GHES or platform-native record, freshness, timeout, containment and service-health behavior; baseline policy; approvals; evidence storage; recovery/restoration.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: No memory injection or consumption command is authorized while Procedure and Criteria remain TBD. Perform only non-mutating topology, capability and baseline discovery. After the owner replaces both TBD fields, submit the completed platform-specific recipe for fresh V3 review; only that contract may define protected allocation, one bounded approved injection/trigger, evidence correlation, recovery and restoration.
revision_candidate.preconditions: TBD fields replaced by a signed recipe; platform/memory topology/tool/target/coverage/consumer/evidence resolved; dedicated non-production SUT and sacrificial data range; stable memory/thermal/power baseline; console/OOB, boot media, storage and recovery proven; every allocation, configuration, injection, consumption, reset, retry and restoration action authorized.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Before authorization: signed platform/tool/spec, topology/target/coverage, allocation/consumer, command, event/timeout, containment, safety and recovery contract. A future reviewed run requires exact identities/hashes, topology and address ownership, baseline audit, per-target command/transcript, fresh target-correlated native uncorrectable-non-fatal record within timeout, prescribed page/process/service containment and counters, proof of no unexpected reset/hang/corruption, memory/system health, recovery/restoration and engineer disposition. Current inventory is readiness evidence only.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Not yet defined. The owner must supply exact NVIDIA/ODM platform memory-RAS criteria. Public Linux documentation identifying an APEI EINJ memory-uncorrectable-non-fatal type and public NVIDIA memory architecture descriptions demonstrate possible mechanisms/topologies only; they do not authorize this case or define PASS.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not assume a DIMM/channel topology, choose an injector from the title, assume EINJ availability, infer or reuse an address, poison live/production/kernel/boot-critical memory, consume an unowned range, clear logs, configure/write an injector, inject, reset, auto-retry or claim PASS/FAIL until a reviewed recipe exists. Stop on any unintended data corruption, fatal escalation, reset, hang, memory loss, thermal/power anomaly or persistent error.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: NVIDIA/ODM FAE and test owner author and approve platform/memory topology, injector, target/coverage, consumer, non-fatal outcome and recovery. Platform/lab owner approves the isolated SUT and sacrificial range. A fresh reviewer approves the executable contract; qualified staff authorize and supervise every later state change, injection and recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Before re-review, an Agent may only collect non-mutating topology/capability inventory and baselines. Humans own recipe creation, protected address allocation, target selection, state changes, injection authorization and recovery. Any future Agent/operator split must come from the newly reviewed contract; engineering retains disposition.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No recovery action is authorized by the current row because no stimulus is authorized. Preserve evidence of any accidental change and escalate. The replacement recipe must define isolation of the affected location, service recovery, optional reboot/power recovery, restoration, clearing policy and final memory-health verification.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Procedure or Criteria remains TBD; product/memory topology/tool/target/coverage/address ownership/consumer/error semantics or expected record is unresolved; only analogous/generic documentation exists; approval, isolated SUT, sacrificial range, baseline, timeout, console, recovery, storage or restoration is missing; capabilities mismatch the signed replacement; or any unreviewed state change, injection or consumption is proposed.

identified_defects: The NV CPU label does not identify the product or host-memory architecture.
V2 assumes DIMM/channel terminology that may not apply to package-integrated NVIDIA CPU memory.
No target/address, trigger/consumer, non-fatal containment, evidence, timeout or recovery is defined.
reason_for_change: Keep the genuine TBD blocker while removing the unsupported DIMM/channel assumption and requiring the memory address, consumption and containment semantics needed to distinguish non-fatal recovery from a crash or silent corruption.

new_technical_evidence.title: NVIDIA Grace Performance Tuning Guide
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Only if the owner identifies the tested NV CPU as Grace
new_technical_evidence.supports: Grace CPU systems use server-class ECC LPDDR5X, including package-integrated configurations, so a generic removable-DIMM target model cannot be presumed.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The source row does not identify Grace or any memory topology.

new_technical_evidence.title: APEI Error INJection
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Linux systems whose firmware exposes the relevant ACPI EINJ capability
new_technical_evidence.supports: The interface lists `0x10` as Memory Uncorrectable non-fatal and explains that memory targeting uses an address/range when supported; advertised types and vendor behavior remain firmware-specific.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The row does not establish EINJ support, address targeting, trigger behavior or acceptance on the intended NVIDIA platform.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-System RAS-00823-V003
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Only this NV CPU memory UCE non-fatal row
new_technical_evidence.supports: The test name/set, generic before/after instructions and literal TBD Procedure/Criteria.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Every executable and acceptance detail is absent.

removed_ambiguities: Does not presume DIMM/channel topology before platform identification.
Requires a protected target address and defined consumer/trigger rather than generic memory injection.
Defines non-fatal as a signed containment/service-health behavior, not merely absence of a fatal label.
Separates safe capability discovery from test completion.
remaining_blockers: Exact platform/memory architecture, Procedure, Criteria, injector, target/coverage, protected address, consumer, expected containment/evidence, timeout and recovery are absent; the test remains BLOCKED.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 retains the correct BLOCKED decision but removes an architecture-specific DIMM assumption and adds the missing address ownership, consumption and containment boundaries needed for a safe non-fatal memory test.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The contract-only validator preserved host-memory UCE non-fatal intent, rejected DIMM and generic-EINJ assumptions, and required explicit product topology, protected address ownership, consumer, coverage and containment before fresh review. It correctly treated inventory as readiness only and made no execution or PASS claim.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 103 names NV CPU memory uncorrectable non-fatal injection but leaves both Procedure and Criteria as literal TBD.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly blocks execution but presumes DIMM/channel targeting before the NVIDIA CPU and memory topology are known.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Permit non-mutating product/topology/capability inventory and baseline export only; prohibit target allocation, injector writes and error consumption until a signed replacement passes fresh review.
